source_text: Anima quae tetigerit morticinum aut a fera captum immunda est. Conversatio mortua immunditiam affert. Separare sanctum ab immundo.
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical purity rules to the soul, explaining that contact with what is dead or captured by a wild beast makes one unclean.
pass_a_gloss: Soul which [has] touched [a] dead [thing] or [a thing] captured by [a] wild [beast] unclean is. [The] way [of life] dead uncleanness brings. To separate [the] holy from [the] unclean.

choices.why: The literal sense of the Latin term for an animal that has died of itself, matching the Levitical purity context.

choices.english: something captured by a wild beast
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of captum and the agency of the wild beast, preserving the ritual category.
rejected: what a wild beast has caught

choices.why: Conversatio means one's manner of life or conduct; rendering it as 'conduct' preserves the moral application Origen is making.
Affert has the sense of carrying or bringing in; 'brings' keeps the active force of the verb.

choices.english: separate the holy from the unclean
choices.why: This is a direct command in the infinitive, echoing Leviticus 10:10; the glossary terms sanctus and immundus are rendered as 'holy' and 'unclean'.
rejected: distinguish the holy from the unclean
set apart the holy from the unclean

bible_refs.note: Anima quae tetigerit morticinum aut a fera captum immunda est

pass_b_english: A soul that has touched a dead body or something captured by a wild beast is unclean (Leviticus 5:2). Dead conduct brings uncleanness. Separate the holy from the unclean (Leviticus 10:10).

last_rejected.why: "Conversatio" means way of life/intercourse, not "conduct" alone; "mortua" modifies it, but "dead conversation/way of life" is the sense—"dead" as spiritually lifeless, not "dead conduct" which is awkward and misses the social/relational sense of conversatio.
last_rejected.fix: A dead way of life brings uncleanness.
last_rejected.ruling: Conversatio can mean 'conduct/way of life'; rendering as 'conduct' is within normal range, not a meaning-changing error.
